code_label: End-to-end QAOA for discrete minimum-variance portfolios
text_span: We present an end-to-end quantum approximate optimisation algorithm (QAOA) to solve the discrete global minimum variance portfolio (DGMVP) model.
rationale: States the paper’s main objective and algorithmic target.

code_label: Discrete trading-lot portfolio formulation
text_span: This model finds a portfolio of risky assets with the lowest possible risk contingent on the number of traded assets being discrete.
rationale: Defines the financial problem setting the algorithm addresses.

code_label: Complete pipeline and noise analysis
text_span: We provide a complete pipeline for this model and analyses its viability for noisy intermediate-scale quantum computers.
rationale: Highlights the end-to-end implementation and hardware-oriented evaluation.

code_label: Layerwise and optimizer benchmarking
text_span: We perform numerical simulations to analyse several optimisation routines, including layerwise optimisation, utilising COYBLA and dual annealing.
rationale: Describes the comparative optimization methodology used in the study.

code_label: Robustness ranking of optimization strategy
text_span: We find dual annealing with a layerwise optimisation routine provides the most robust performance.
rationale: Summarizes a key empirical finding about the best-performing optimization setup.

code_label: Thermal noise blocks quantum advantage
text_span: We observe that realistic thermal relaxation noise levels preclude quantum advantage.
rationale: States a major negative result about near-term hardware noise.

code_label: Measurement noise may dominate later
text_span: However, stochastic measurement noise will dominate when hardware sufficiently improves.
rationale: Identifies a regime where a different noise source becomes limiting.

code_label: Favourable shot-scaling indication
text_span: Within this regime, we numerically demonstrate a favourable scaling in the number of shots required to obtain the global minimum—an indication of quantum advantage in portfolio optimisation.
rationale: Reports the paper’s main positive scaling observation.

code_label: General QAOA framing
text_span: To avoid ambiguity, we use the QAOA to represent the general QAOA in the rest of this article
rationale: Clarifies the algorithmic framework used throughout the paper.

code_label: Binary block encoding reduces qubit use
text_span: As block sizes increase, the binary encoding method will use exponentially fewer qubits than the one-hot encoding method
rationale: Motivates the chosen encoding strategy on resource grounds.

code_label: Warm-start and max-biased initial states prioritized
text_span: Experiments in Appx. C show max-biased state and ranked warm-started state outperform other methods.
rationale: Identifies the initial states selected for the main analysis.

code_label: Warm-start construction from rounded continuous solution
text_span: A ranked warm-started state |w⟩ws of the DGMVP model prepares the asset weights as
rationale: Introduces the warm-start initialization procedure.

code_label: Dense cost circuit with linear depth
text_span: Thus, a dense quantum circuit can be constructed with O(N) depth, where N is the number of qubits
rationale: States the circuit-depth scaling of the cost operator implementation.

code_label: Hard mixer preserves budget constraint
text_span: In this section, we design a hard mixing operator based on the qubit excitation operators to conserve the budget constraint in the QAOA optimisation.
rationale: Explains the purpose of the custom mixer.

code_label: Quantum bridge phenomenon
text_span: we denote as the quantum bridge outlined in Appx. E.
rationale: Names a structural phenomenon used to justify the mixer design.

code_label: Nearest-neighbour mixer chosen for performance and gates
text_span: we use ˆ M1(β) as the mixing operator due to its better performance in the optimisation
rationale: States the default mixer choice and why it was selected.

code_label: DA outperforms COBYLA under stochastic noise
text_span: DA still stops at a region close to the optimal parameter.
rationale: Supports the claim that dual annealing is more robust than COBYLA.

code_label: Layerwise optimization improves performance
text_span: layerwise optimisation methods, frozen-layerwise and unfrozen-layerwise for our ansatz.
rationale: Introduces the layerwise training strategies evaluated in the paper.

code_label: Unfrozen layerwise generally best
text_span: we observe that unfrozen-layerwise optimisation, in general, outperforms frozen-layerwise in both αmean and αmin.
rationale: Reports the comparative outcome of the layerwise methods.

code_label: Unfrozen layerwise with DA exceeds 80 percent global-minimum success
text_span: the unfrozen-layerwise approach using DA returns the global minimum with a probability greater than 80% for p ≥3
rationale: Quantifies the best-performing optimization configuration.

code_label: Scaling analysis uses exact statevector to remove shot noise
text_span: we rebuild the parameterised quantum circuit using a statevector representation and calculate the exact expectation value ⟨C⟩.
rationale: Describes the methodological choice for scaling studies.

code_label: Quantum algorithm beats maxbias on approximation ratios
text_span: our quantum algorithm achieves a significantly lower αk% mean for all tested k and αmin compared to the maxbias method
rationale: Summarizes the main scaling result against a classical baseline.

code_label: Warm-start optimization skews distribution toward global minimum
text_span: we find that while the optimisation increases the mean, it also skews the distribution towards the global minimum.
rationale: Captures the nuanced effect of optimization on the warm-started state.

code_label: Global minimum probability scaling fit
text_span: we fit the inverse of the mean of Pgm (the crosses in Fig. 11) with the function 1/¯Pgm = a · B(n, l)b
rationale: Describes the fitted scaling model used to assess advantage.

code_label: Warm-start scaling exponent suggests favorable asymptotics
text_span: we find b = 0.76 ± 0.30 for the warm-started initial state
rationale: Reports the fitted exponent for one scaling regime.

code_label: Maxbias scaling exponent suggests stronger improvement
text_span: and b = 0.51 ± 0.09 for the maxbias initial state
rationale: Reports the fitted exponent for the other scaling regime.

code_label: Thermal relaxation noise degrades optimization
text_span: our algorithm performs poorly in the presence of thermal relaxation noise.
rationale: States a key hardware-related limitation.

code_label: Post-selection partially mitigates noise
text_span: The impact can be mitigated by post-selecting out states not within the constrained feasible region.
rationale: Describes the mitigation strategy used under noise.

code_label: Post-selection increases measurement burden
text_span: post-selection requires significantly more measurements to maintain a constant stochastic noise in the presence of quantum noise.
rationale: Identifies a trade-off introduced by the mitigation method.

code_label: Fault tolerance or lower error rates needed
text_span: This indicates drastic improvements in error rates or fault-tolerant quantum computation will be required for viable quantum finance applications.
rationale: States the paper’s forward-looking requirement for practical viability.

code_label: Warm-started state can approach classical optimum
text_span: the warm-started initial state approaches the global minimum.
rationale: Summarizes the warm-start behavior in the scaling discussion.

code_label: Quantum advantage remains conditional
text_span: may asymptotically (in n and l) outperform the classical method in the number of samples required to find the DGMVP solution.
rationale: Captures the paper’s conditional asymptotic advantage claim.

code_label: Quantum bridge on two-qubit excitations
text_span: we name this phenomenon as the quantum bridge on two-qubit excitations.
rationale: Names the appendix phenomenon used to justify operator composition.

code_label: Quantum bridge on three-qubit excitations
text_span: we name this phenomenon as the quantum bridge on three-qubit excitations.
rationale: Names the analogous three-qubit phenomenon.

code_label: Mixer with smaller L is easier to optimize
text_span: the ansatz becomes harder to optimise in the presence of stochastic measurement errors when using ˆ M2(β) compared to ˆ M1(β)
rationale: Supports the choice of nearest-neighbour mixing over longer-range mixing.

code_label: DA uses fewer cost-function accesses than COBYLA
text_span: DA uses fewer total cost function accesses than COBYLA to achieve smaller values of αmin and αmean in the large p regime.
rationale: Summarizes the optimizer comparison in the appendix.

code_label: Chosen DA hyperparameters are a trade-off
text_span: the choice of I = 2000 and Nm = 16 for DA is a good trade-off between the optimisation costs
rationale: States the selected hyperparameter setting and its rationale.

code_label: Warm-start scaling may asymptotically outperform classical sampling
text_span: the warm-started initial state may asymptotically (in n and l) outperform the classical method in the number of samples required to find the DGMVP solution.
rationale: Captures the paper’s concluding asymptotic claim.
